title: Chapter 85 — The Follow-Up System: Architecture of the Second Yes
intro: The pipeline pools operationalised and the sequence library.

sections.title: Most Sales Die of Silence
sections.content:
Most appliance quotes die of silence, not rejection. The data says it takes 3-5 touches to close a quote that walked out. Most salespeople follow up once and quit.

The follow-up system is not optional. It is the architecture that turns a 15 percent walk-out conversion rate into a 35 percent conversion rate. That difference alone can add $50,000 to your annual income.

Think of your pipeline as three pools: active quotes (quoted in the last 14 days), aging quotes (15-30 days), and long-cycle (30-90 days). Each pool needs a different touch cadence and a different message strategy.

sections.title: The Sequence Library
sections.content:
Day 0 — same-day thank-you text within 2 hours: 'Hi [name], great meeting you today. Your quote for the [product] is in your email. Text me anytime with questions.'

Day 1 — formal quote email with images and specs. Day 3 — phone call, not text. 'Any questions that came up? Did you get a chance to discuss with your partner?'

Day 7 — value-add: comparison chart, review article, installation video. Something that gives them new information, not just a reminder that you exist.

Day 14 — honest check-in with promo deadline reminder. Day 30 — long-game touch: 'I know life gets busy. I am here whenever you are ready.'

Every touch must add information the customer did not have. Never 'just checking in' — that phrase communicates zero value and tells the customer you have nothing new to offer.

sections.title: The CRM Is the System
sections.content:
Log every touch. Tag the reason for no-close: price, spouse, timing, competition, product uncertainty. Set the next follow-up date before you close the current one.

The patterns in your CRM tell you where your floor process is breaking. If 80 percent of your stalled quotes are price objections, your value presentation needs work. If 60 percent are spouse delays, your kitchen-table kit needs upgrading. If most quotes stall at day 7 and never convert, your value-add touches are not compelling enough.

The CRM is not an admin tool. It is your coaching tool and your income accelerator. The data tells you exactly where to focus your improvement efforts.
